test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 12 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The average runs scored by a batsman in 23 matches is 40. In the next 10 matches, the batsman scored an average of 16 runs. Find his average runs scored (rounded off to two decimals) in all the 33 matches.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume the base average for all 33 matches is 40.

Deviation for the next 10 matches = 16 − 40 = −24 per match.

Total deviation = 10 × −24 = −240.

Change in overall average = −240 ÷ 33 = −7.2727... ≈ −7.27.

New combined average = 40 − 7.27 = 32.73.

**∴ The correct answer is 32.73 runs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average runs for the first 23 matches = 40

Average runs for the next 10 matches = 16

**Formula Used:**

Combined Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 
 23 matches
 Average = 40
 
 10 matches
 Average = 16
 

 Combined 33 matches | Average = 32.73

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total runs in the first 23 matches = 23 × 40 = 920

⇒ Total runs in the next 10 matches = 10 × 16 = 160

⇒ Total runs in all 33 matches = 920 + 160 = 1080

⇒ Combined Average = 1080 ÷ 33 = 360 ÷ 11

⇒ Combined Average = 32.7272... ≈ 32.73

**∴ The correct answer is 32.73 runs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

When dealing with groups of different sizes, the combined average is calculated as Aw = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Net Deviation Method

Instead of multiplying large numbers, assume a base average and calculate the net deviation. True Average = Assumed Average + (Net Deviation ÷ Total Count). This makes calculations significantly faster.
